note: Scans recognized throughput rows in primary release JSON artifacts for 1 GiB+ full-string JavaScript rows that meet the 200 MiB/s bounded-memory counterexample rule. This is a guard over existing artifacts, not a new benchmark run or a runtime-limit proof.

findings.summary: No recognized release row currently meets the 200 MiB/s bounded full-string JS rule.
22 recognized 1 GiB+ partial/projection JavaScript row(s) reach the threshold but are not full-string StAX counterexamples.
3 recognized 1 GiB+ near-full row(s) cross the threshold only after omitting text/CDATA string materialization.

91 recognized 1 GiB+ full-string JavaScript row(s) fail the bounded-memory counterexample criterion: 91 explicit boundedMemory=false, 0 bounded flag without row-level memory proof, 0 unknown bounded flag.
767 recognized measured row(s) include fullStringParity and boundedMemory classifications; 0 have unknown fullStringParity and 20 have unknown boundedMemory.
Cross-process aggregate rows are reported separately from individual sample rows so fastest-row triage does not hide average-throughput evidence.
